sources.title: 쉬운 공문서 쓰기 길잡이
sources.author: National Institute of Korean Language (국립국어원)
sources.accessScope: Official item description and reuse notice; PDF foreword, contents and printed/PDF pp.8,12,15,21–23 visually inspected; extracted text pp.28–32 read. Most image-only pages were not inspected.
sources.rights: Item states KOGL Type3 (attribution/no derivatives). No guide text, adapted examples, page images, or translated checklist redistributed. These are independently worded operational rules about underlying language principles with synthetic examples; not an official NIKL skill.

rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code, including obligation versus permission.
rules.rationale: Project meaning-preservation requirement, independent of any editorial source.

rules.intent: Resolve ambiguous referents without guessing. Preserve the scope of exclusive and universal particles: in the proposed wording, a shared predicate must be true of every named group and each stated example must respect that scope.
rules.rationale: Extends the guide’s sentence agreement and grammatical-accuracy guidance to explanatory editing; examples and operational questions are original.
exceptions: Keep an omitted subject when context is unambiguous.
If the actor or modifier scope is unknown, flag it rather than invent it.

rules.intent: Preserve or follow the requested speech level; maintain distinctions among 의무, 허용, 가능성, and prohibition when revising endings. Keep the period and tense of a past permission or duty clear to a reader encountering the text on its own.
rules.rationale: The guide discusses audience-facing endings; preserving task-selected register and modal force is a project adaptation, not a mandated public-document register.
exceptions: Quoted wording and exact UI labels retain their form.
A legal duty must not become an optional request merely to sound polite.

rules.intent: Explain unfamiliar Korean or borrowed terms where needed; simplify only with equivalent meaning and preserve exact technical/legal names.
rules.rationale: Applies reader-oriented terminology principles from pp.8 and12; it does not import the guide’s substitution tables.
exceptions: Use a precise specialist term for an audience that needs it.
A familiar Sino-Korean word need not be replaced because of its origin.

rules.intent: Repair predicate agreement and preserve each condition when splitting sentences. In a requested comparison, give each group a separate entry with its numerical result and unit when asked, reasons, and any explicit exemption. State any duty shared by the groups.
rules.rationale: Original operational interpretation of pp.15 and28–32 about visible organization and grammatical accuracy. English active-voice and word-count rules do not transfer literally.
exceptions: Korean passive/causative forms can express necessary meaning.
Preserve condition, exception, and negation scope through any split.
